text: Writing clean code is a skill that benefits both you and your team. The main goal is readability—making your code easy for others (and your future self) to understand. Start with clear naming conventions: use descriptive names for variables, like `totalPrice` instead of `tp`. Break your program into small, focused functions that do one thing well. This not only simplifies testing but also makes your code more maintainable, since you can fix or update a single function without rewriting the whole program. Ultimately, clean code saves time and reduces frustration.
